**2.0 SAFETY & SAFETY PERFORMANCE**

2.1 K. Barnes reported on the September safety statistics to date. There have been two (2) reported near misses this week, both related to track worker movements in the vicinity of active roads. No injuries. Both incidents are under investigation.

2.2 The Board noted the completion of the Level Crossing LX-22 cable strike investigation. Root cause: third-party contractor operating outside agreed corridor. **Decision: A formal letter of demand will be issued to the contractor for cost recovery. Owner: K. Barnes. Due: 18/09/2026.**

---

**3.0 PROJECT PRIORITISATION & SCHEDULING**

3.1 **Review of Project Pipeline**

The Board reviewed the current portfolio of works scheduled for the remainder of the 2026 calendar year and into Q1 2027. The focus was on resource availability, network access windows, and interdependencies.

3.2 **Ballast Replacement Project (BRP)**

The Chair called for an update on the Ballast Replacement Project. L. Tran advised that the project remains a high priority for the Board due to its impact on line speed restrictions and track stability in the Hunter Valley corridor.

After discussion, the Board formally confirmed the **current scheduled completion date** for the Ballast Replacement Project. The Ballast Replacement Project scheduled_completion_date is 2026-09-18. Record status: current. This date is confirmed as current and is the target against which all project milestones are being tracked. There is no change to this date at this time.

L. Tran noted that the major constraint is the availability of the high-output ballast tamper. A confirmation of availability is still pending from the depot (Action 04/09-02). The project team is currently working on the assumption that the tamper will be available from 14 September. If this is not confirmed by Monday, a contingency plan will be activated. The contingency involves using a smaller, slower tamper which will extend the works programme by approximately four (4) days.

**Decision:** The Board endorsed the approach to continue with the current date of 18/09/2026 and requested L. Tran to provide a definitive update on the tamper availability at the next meeting, or earlier if required.

3.3 **Signalling Upgrade – Sector 7**

R. Singh provided an update on the signalling upgrade works. The project is on track for its scheduled completion in late November. The main risk identified is the delivery of the new interlocking modules, which are currently in transit from the manufacturer. A revised delivery date of 25 September has been provided by the supplier. R. Singh will monitor this closely.

3.4 **Overhead Traction – Insulator Replacement Program**

A. Petrova reported that the insulator replacement program is progressing well. Works are currently 65% complete. The program is scheduled to be completed by mid-October. No resource issues are anticipated.

**1530 – Whiteboard update.** I’ve added the following:
- Friday 0900 – hopper load at quarry (position by 0830)
- Friday – submit TAP for Moss Vale platform edge repair
- Berrima drain work – closed (TAP active until 1700 today)

**1545 – WHS check.** I reviewed the site diary entries from the drain crew – they noted the dead sheep removal and the silt clearing. All good. I’ve also filed a copy of the environmental sheet from the oil change in the WHS folder.

**1600 – Brief from the night crew.** The night shift coordinator (T. Okafor) came in early for a quick handover. I’ve given him the key points:
- Drain work at Berrima – closed, TAP active until 1700
- Hopper load on Friday – position by 0830
- Vehicle oil leak – booked for service
- Point machine oil change – complete, logged

**1615 – Final check of the portal.** No new permits. I’ve also checked the weather radar – there’s a chance of a storm later, but nothing that should affect the line. I’ll note it in the handover.

**1630 – End of shift.** Handover notes written, whiteboard updated, and all logs completed. I’m off. – M. Chen
**1750 – Walkaround of the yard.** Did a quick check of the vehicles and equipment before dark. Noticed the following:
- Utility 3 – front left tyre looks a bit low. Will check pressure and top up.
- Hopper – still in the yard, waiting for Friday. I gave it a quick once-over myself since the loader operator hasn’t been in yet. The weld patch on the side looks intact, but there’s a bit of surface rust forming near the top edge. Not a safety issue, but I’ll note it for the crew to inspect before the load.
- Point machine – the oil change from earlier today is logged. I’ve had a look at the seals, they look fine.

**1815 – Radio check.** All good. Crew members on the line tonight: two patrollers (A. Mears and J. O’Brien) doing a routine track inspection between Moss Vale and Bowral. No other work scheduled for tonight, so it should be a quiet shift.

**1830 – Email check.** No new urgent items. There’s a notice from NOC about a signalling test on the 12th at Goulburn – not our line, but I’ve filed it in the comms folder as per the usual process.

**1845 – Weather update.** Radar shows a band of storms forming to the west, moving east. ETA around 2100-2200. I’ll let the patrollers know to keep an eye on the sky and take shelter if needed. Not expecting any washouts, but we’ll see.

**1900 – Patroller update.** A. Mears called in from the Moss Vale end. All clear so far. No debris on the track, no unusual noise from the rails. He’s continuing towards Bowral. J. O’Brien is working the other direction. I’ve asked them to check the culvert near the Berrima work site while they’re out there – just to make sure the recent rain hasn’t caused any new scouring.

**1930 – Tyre pressure.** Topped up Utility 3’s front left tyre. It was at 28 psi, now at 32. I’ve logged it in the vehicle book. Will mention it again in the morning so someone can check for a slow leak.

**1945 – Hopper note.** I’ve added a handwritten note to the hopper inspection sheet: “Check rust on top edge before Friday load.” The loader operator will see it when they come in. Also, I’ve confirmed the positioning time of 0830 with L. Nguyen again – she’s aware of the hopper’s condition and said it’s fine as long as the weld holds. I’ve told her we’ll do a final check on Friday morning.

**2000 – Whiteboard update.** I’ve added the following:
- Berrima drain work – closed (TAP surrendered)
- Hopper load on Friday – position by 0830, check rust on top edge
- Utility 3 – tyre topped up, monitor for slow leak
- Storms possible later – patrollers advised

**2015 – Brief from the night crew.** Tom Okafor shift_start_time is 06:30. Record status: current. I’ve noted this in the handover book for the morning shift – I’ll be finishing at 0100, so the early start is for tomorrow’s day shift. Just want to make sure it’s clear in the log. I’ve also added a note for the morning coordinator to check the hopper’s rust spot before the crew leaves for the quarry.

**2030 – Radio check with patrollers.** Both are still out on the track. No issues. J. O’Brien mentioned a dead kangaroo near the crossing at Wingello – he’s moved it off the track, but I’ll note it for the morning crew to arrange removal if it’s still there.

**2045 – Storm update.** Radar shows the storm band is now closer than expected. It’s about 30 minutes out. I’ve called both patrollers to suggest they wrap up their current section and head back to the vehicles. No need to be out in the open if lightning starts.

**2100 – Patrollers back.** Both are back at the vehicles. A. Mears reported a small tree branch on the track near the Berrima culvert – he’s removed it. No other issues. They’ll wait out the storm in the vehicles and resume once it passes.

**2115 – Storm hit.** Rain is heavy, some wind. No lightning strikes reported near the line so far. I’m monitoring the weather radar and the track condition reports. Will update the handover if anything changes.

**2130 – NOC call.** NOC called to check on the storm situation. I’ve confirmed no issues on our section. They’ve asked me to report any washouts or debris immediately. I’ve noted their contact number on the whiteboard.

**2200 – Storm passing.** Rain is easing. I’ve asked the patrollers to do a quick visual check of the track once the rain stops, just to make sure there’s no debris or washouts. They’ll call back in 30 minutes with an update.

**2230 – Patroller update.** All clear after the storm. No debris, no washouts. A. Mears checked the culvert near the Berrima site – water is flowing normally, no new scouring. Good. I’ve logged this in the site diary.
**Shift Log – Southern Highlands Line**
**Date: 09/09/2026 (Wednesday)**
**Log Keeper: Margaret Chen (Night Shift 1800–0100)**
**Weather: Storm passed ~2200, clearing, 19C at time of writing**

---

**2245 – Handover book update.** Morning coordinator confirmed receipt of the hopper note. I’ve also updated the whiteboard with the patroller all-clear from 2230. No further action needed tonight unless the storm returns.

**2300 – Track Access Permit (TAP) review for tomorrow.** I’ve pulled up the permit list for the day shift. Three permits are active for 10/09:

- TAP-1187 (Goulburn–Moss Vale, ballast tamping) – On track for 0630 start.
- TAP-1192 (Berrima culvert inspection) – Pending weather sign-off. If the culvert shows any new scouring overnight, the morning crew will need to re-inspect before issuing.
- TAP-1195 (Wingello crossing repair) – Booked for arvo, pending materials delivery.

I’ve left a note for the day coordinator to double-check the TAP-1192 weather condition before the crew leaves. The culvert looked fine at 2230, but the storm was heavier than forecast.

**2315 – Crew assignment check for 10/09.** Lena Fischer is on the day shift for the ballast tamping crew. Shift start time is 06:30. Lena Fischer shift_start_time is 06:30. Record status: current. I’ve confirmed this against the roster and noted it in the handover book – the crew will be leaving the depot at 0615 to be on site by 0630. Also confirmed that the tamping machine is fuelled and ready; the operator reported no issues at end of shift yesterday.

**2330 – Equipment status update.** The following checks were done at the end of the night shift:

- Tamping machine (TAM-03) – Fuel full, hydraulic fluid at minimum mark. Topped up. No leaks noted.
- Hi-rail vehicle (HRV-02) – Tyre pressure checked, all good. Radio battery low – replaced.
- Portable generator (GEN-04) – Not used tonight. No issues.

I’ve logged these in the equipment book. The generator hasn’t been run in a while – might be worth a test run tomorrow if the crew has time.

**2345 – Wingello crossing check.** I drove past the crossing on my way back from the Berrima culvert check. The dead kangaroo is still there, just off the track. I’ve flagged it for the morning crew to arrange removal before the repair crew arrives. It’s not obstructing the track, but it’s close enough that it could attract scavengers and become a hazard if the crew is working nearby.

**0000 – Night patrol check-in.** Both patrollers have completed their post-storm visual checks. No debris, no washouts, no new scouring at the culvert. They’re heading back to the depot now. I’ve logged their completion in the site diary and will include it in the handover.

**0015 – Weather update.** Radar shows the storm band has moved east of our section. No further rain expected overnight. Temperature dropping to around 15C. I’ve noted this on the whiteboard for the morning crew – should be a clear start for the day shift.

**0030 – NOC re-check.** NOC called to confirm the all-clear from the patrollers. I’ve passed on the details from the 2230 and 0000 checks. They’ve noted it in their log. No further action required.

**0045 – Handover prep.** I’ve written the handover notes for the day coordinator. Key items:

1. Hopper rust spot – check before crew leaves for quarry.
2. TAP-1192 weather sign-off required before culvert inspection.
3. Wingello crossing – dead kangaroo removal needed.
4. Lena Fischer shift start 06:30 – confirmed with roster.
5. Generator GEN-04 – test run recommended.

I’ve also added a note about the radio battery replacement – HRV-02 is ready for use.

**0100 – End of shift.** All clear. No incidents. Handover book signed. Day coordinator will be in at 0530.

---

**Margin note (handwritten):** Check hopper first thing – rust spot looked worse in the morning light. Also remind crew about the kangaroo – don’t want it there when the repair crew arrives.

---

**Morning handover (added by M. Chen at 0105, before leaving):**
1. **Hopper rust spot** – check before crew leaves for quarry. J. Okafor’s margin note says it looked worse in the morning light. I’ll have the crew do a visual inspection and photo before they load.
2. **TAP-1192** – weather sign-off required before the culvert inspection can proceed. The storm has cleared, so this should be straightforward once the NOC confirms the all-clear.
3. **Wingello crossing** – dead kangaroo removal. I’ve called the local council’s road maintenance line – they’ve got a crew in the area this morning and will swing by. I’ll follow up if it’s not done by 1000.
4. **Lena Fischer** – shift start 06:30, confirmed with roster.
5. **Generator GEN-04** – test run recommended. I’ll schedule this for the arvo when the crew is back from the quarry.

**0545 – Radio check.** All radios are charged and accounted for. HRV-02 is ready for use.

---

**0600 – Weather update.** Radar is clear. No rain expected for the next 24 hours. Temperature forecast to reach 24C by midday. Good conditions for the culvert inspection and the quarry run.

**0615 – Crew briefing (day shift).** I’ve briefed the crew on the day’s plan:

- **Culvert inspection** – TAP-1192 weather sign-off pending. Once the NOC confirms, the inspection crew will head to the Berrima culvert. The night patrol found no new scouring, so this is a routine inspection.
- **Quarry run** – Hopper needs a check first. Crew will do the visual inspection and photo before loading. If the rust spot is worse than expected, we may need to delay the run and get a welder out.
- **Wingello crossing** – Council crew is on it. If they don’t show by 1000, I’ll call again.

**0630 – Lena Fischer arrived.** She’s on the culvert inspection crew today. I’ve given her the TAP-1192 details and the weather sign-off requirement. She’s aware that the NOC needs to confirm before they head out.

---

**0645 – NOC call.** Spoke with the Network Operations Centre about TAP-1192. They’ve confirmed the weather window is clear and the permit is approved for today. The Network Operations Centre permit_approval_date is 2026-09-08, so the sign-off is valid. I’ve noted this on the TAP-1192 form and in the site diary. The culvert inspection crew can proceed.

**0650 – Updated the whiteboard.** TAP-1192 weather sign-off received. Culvert inspection is a go. Crew is preparing to leave.

---

**0700 – Hopper check.** Crew did the visual inspection of the hopper before loading. The rust spot is still there but doesn’t look worse than yesterday. Photos taken and logged. They’ve decided to proceed with the quarry run but will keep an eye on it. I’ve noted that a proper weld inspection should be scheduled for next week – I’ll add it to the maintenance calendar.

The Network Operations Centre permit_approval_date is 2026-09-08. Record status: historical.

**0715 – Quarry run underway.** Crew left for the quarry at 0710. ETA back on site is around 1100, assuming no delays at the weighbridge. I’ve asked them to radio in when they’re loaded.

**0725 – Wingello crossing follow-up.** No word from the council crew yet. I’ve left a message with their dispatch. I’ll try again at 1000 if I don’t hear back.

---

**0730 – Generator GEN-04 test run.** I’ve scheduled this for 1330 this afternoon. The generator is in the equipment shed, and the test should take about 30 minutes. I’ll need someone to log the run time and fuel level. I’ve put a note on the board for the crew.

**0745 – Site diary update.** Logged the NOC confirmation for TAP-1192, the hopper check results, and the quarry run departure. Also noted the council follow-up for the kangaroo.

**0800 – Morning tea.** No issues. The crew is out on the quarry run, and the culvert inspection crew is on site at Berrima. I’m holding the fort in the office.

---

**0830 – Culvert inspection update.** Lena called in from Berrima. The culvert looks clear, no new scouring. They’re doing the photo documentation now and will be back on site by 1000. I’ve logged this in the site diary.

**0845 – Council call.** I tried the council again about the kangaroo. Their dispatch said the crew is running late but will be at Wingello by 1030. I’ve noted this and will follow up if it’s not done by 1100.

---

**0900 – Radio check.** All good. No issues with the radios. HRV-02 is working fine after the battery replacement.
**0915 – Quarry run check.** Radioed the crew. They’re at the weighbridge now, about 10 minutes out from loading. No issues reported. ETA back on site still around 1100.

**0930 – Berrima culvert crew back.** Lena and Dave arrived back on site. They’ve got the photos and the inspection sheet done. Culvert is clear, no new scouring, no debris build-up. I’ve filed the photos in the shared drive under /Berrima/Culvert/2026-09-10. Lena mentioned the grate at the inlet has a loose bolt – she’s added it to the defects list. Not urgent, but worth tightening before the next heavy rain. I’ll add it to next week’s minor works.

**0945 – Wingello crossing.** Still no council crew. I called their dispatch again – they said the crew is en route but got delayed at another job. They’re aiming for 1100 now. I’ve noted this in the diary. If they don’t show by 1130, I’ll escalate to the council supervisor directly.

---

**1000 – Permit check.** TAP-1192 is still current and valid for the day. No changes from NOC. I’ve done a quick review of the permit conditions – all good, no restrictions that affect our current work. The culvert inspection was done under this permit, and the quarry run is covered by it too. I’ve logged the times in the permit register.

**1015 – Equipment shed tidy-up.** I’ve started clearing the bench near the door. There’s a few old parts and some empty oil containers that need to go to the recycling bin. I’ll finish this arvo when things quiet down. Nothing urgent, just housekeeping.

**1030 – Radio check.** All good. HRV-02 still working fine. No issues with the handhelds either.

---

**1100 – Quarry run ETA.** Crew radioed in – they’re loaded and heading back. Should be on site by 1130. They mentioned the hopper is handling okay, no wobble or anything. I’ll do a quick visual check when they arrive.

**1115 – Council call.** Tried the council again. Their dispatch said the crew is at Wingello now, doing the crossing. Should be done within the hour. I’ll follow up if I don’t hear anything by 1230.

**1130 – Quarry run arrival.** Crew back on site. Hopper loaded with 14 tonnes of crushed rock. Weighbridge ticket is in the glovebox of the ute – I’ll log it in the delivery register. They’ve parked the ute near the shed. I’ve done a quick visual on the hopper – rust spot looks the same, no new cracks. Photos taken and logged.

---

**1145 – Lunch break.** Crew is having lunch now. No issues. I’m doing the site diary update while they eat.

**1200 – Site diary update.** Logged the quarry run arrival, the weighbridge ticket number (WB-22014), the council update, and the Berrima culvert inspection results. Also noted the loose bolt on the inlet grate for next week’s minor works.

**1215 – Generator GEN-04 prep.** I’ve pulled the generator out of the shed and checked the fuel level – it’s about half full. I’ll top it up before the test run at 1330. Also checked the oil – looks clean. I’ve put the test sheet on the clipboard near the shed door.

---

**1230 – Council follow-up.** No word from the council crew yet. I’ve left a message with their dispatch again. I’ll try the supervisor directly at 1300 if I don’t hear back.

**1245 – Radio check.** All good. No issues.

---

**1300 – Council supervisor call.** Spoke to the supervisor directly. He said the crew is finishing up at Wingello now and will be done by 1330. He’s confirmed they’ll call us when they’re done. I’ve noted this in the diary.

**1315 – Hopper check.** Did a quick visual on the hopper before the crew starts unloading. The rust spot is still there, no change. I’ve noted that the weld inspection should be scheduled for next week – I’ll add it to the maintenance calendar on Monday.

**1330 – Generator GEN-04 test run.** Started the generator. It’s running smoothly, no unusual noises. I’ve logged the start time and the fuel level (half full). The test will run for 30 minutes. I’ll log the end time and fuel level at 1400.

---

**1345 – Wingello crossing.** Council crew called – they’re done at Wingello. The crossing is clear and they’ve removed the debris. I’ve logged this in the diary and closed the follow-up.
**Southern Highlands Line – Shift Log**
**Date:** Tuesday 15 September 2026
**Shift:** Day (0600 – 1800)
**Log Keeper:** Margaret Chen
**Weather:** Fine, becoming hot. 32C at 0900, forecast top 36C this arvo. No rain expected.

---

**1400 – Generator GEN-04 test run complete.** Stopped the generator. Ran for 30 minutes without issue. Fuel level checked – still reads about half, slight drop only. Logged end time and fuel level on the test sheet. Generator returned to the shed, lead and plug coiled. Test sheet left on the clipboard for the supervisor to sign off tomorrow.

**1415 – Berrima culvert – loose bolt.** As noted earlier, the inlet grate has a loose bolt. I’ve flagged it for next week’s minor works. No action required today – the grate is secure enough, just needs a tighten. Added to the maintenance calendar for Monday 21st. Not urgent.

**1430 – Quarry run – unloading complete.** The crew has finished unloading the ballast from the morning delivery. Hopper is now about three-quarters full. I did another quick visual on the hopper – the rust spot is still the same, no new cracks or flaking. The weld inspection for next week is still on the calendar – I’ll confirm the date with the supervisor on Monday.

**1445 – Radio check.** All good. No issues.

---

**1500 – Site walk – Wingello crossing.** Since the council crew finished at 1345, I drove out to Wingello to have a look at the crossing myself. The debris has been removed and the crossing surface looks clean. The council crew did a good job – no signs of damage to the rails or the crossing plates. I’ve logged this in the diary and closed the follow-up. No further action needed.

**1530 – Returned to depot.** No issues on the drive back. Road conditions are dry, dust is a bit of an issue but nothing major.

---

**1545 – Phone call – Network Operations Centre (NOC).** Received a call from the NOC regarding the track access permit (TAP) for tomorrow’s planned work at the Mittagong loop. They’ve asked us to confirm the start time and the crew size. I’ve confirmed 0700 start, crew of four. The TAP number is TAP-2026-0916-02. The NOC has logged this. No changes to the permit.

**1600 – Permit check.** I’ve reviewed the TAP for tomorrow – TAP-2026-0916-02 – and it’s still current and valid. The permit covers the Mittagong loop from 0700 to 1500. All conditions are met. I’ve noted this in the diary and filed the copy in the permit folder.

---

**1615 – Tool inventory – quick count.** Did a quick count of the hand tools in the shed. All present and accounted for. The new torque wrench is still in its box – I’ll log it in the tool register tomorrow when I have time. The old torque wrench is in the drawer, marked for calibration. I’ve left a note on the shed door to remind the crew not to use it until it’s been calibrated.

**1630 – Water refill.** Topped up the water tank on the ute. It was getting low. Also checked the oil – fine. Tyre pressure looks good. No issues.

---

**1645 – Site diary update.** Logged the following for today:
- Generator GEN-04 test run – completed, no issues.
- Wingello crossing – council crew finished, debris removed, crossing clear.
- Quarry run – unloading complete, hopper three-quarters full.
- Berrima culvert – loose bolt flagged for next week’s minor works.
- TAP-2026-0916-02 confirmed with NOC for tomorrow.
- Tool inventory – all present, old torque wrench marked for calibration.

**1700 – Handover notes started.** I’m starting the handover notes for the night shift. The night crew is due at 1730. I’ll leave a summary on the whiteboard in the shed and a more detailed note in the diary.

---

**1715 – Night crew arrival.** The night shift crew has arrived – Dave and Simon. I’ve given them a quick briefing:
- Hopper is three-quarters full. No unloading planned overnight.
- Generator GEN-04 is back in the shed, test run completed today.
- Wingello crossing is clear – council work done.
- TAP for tomorrow is confirmed – TAP-2026-0916-02, 0700 start.
- Old torque wrench is out of service – do not use.
- Loose bolt on Berrima culvert inlet grate – flagged for next week, no action needed overnight.

documents.content:
---

**2.0 SAFETY & SAFETY PERFORMANCE**

2.1 K. Barnes reported on the September safety statistics to date. There have been two (2) reported near misses this week, both related to track worker movements in the vicinity of active roads. No injuries. Both incidents are under investigation.

2.2 The Board noted the completion of the Level Crossing LX-22 cable strike investigation. Root cause: third-party contractor operating outside agreed corridor. **Decision: A formal letter of demand will be issued to the contractor for cost recovery. Owner: K. Barnes. Due: 18/09/2026.**

2.3 A safety bulletin regarding the correct use of lookout working in wet weather is to be issued. Owner: K. Barnes. Due: 14/09/2026.

---

**3.0 PROJECT PRIORITISATION & SCHEDULING**

3.1 **Review of Project Pipeline**

The Board reviewed the current portfolio of works scheduled for the remainder of the 2026 calendar year and into Q1 2027. The focus was on resource availability, network access windows, and interdependencies.

3.2 **Ballast Replacement Project (BRP)**

The Chair called for an update on the Ballast Replacement Project. L. Tran advised that the project remains a high priority for the Board due to its impact on line speed restrictions and track stability in the Hunter Valley corridor.

After discussion, the Board formally confirmed the **current scheduled completion date** for the Ballast Replacement Project. The Ballast Replacement Project scheduled_completion_date is 2026-09-18. Record status: current. This date is confirmed as current and is the target against which all project milestones are being tracked. There is no change to this date at this time.

L. Tran noted that the major constraint is the availability of the high-output ballast tamper. A confirmation of availability is still pending from the depot (Action 04/09-02). The project team is currently working on the assumption that the tamper will be available from 14 September. If this is not confirmed by Monday, a contingency plan will be activated. The contingency involves using a smaller, slower tamper which will extend the works programme by approximately four (4) days.

**Decision:** The Board endorsed the approach to continue with the current date of 18/09/2026 and requested L. Tran to provide a definitive update on the tamper availability at the next meeting, or earlier if required.

3.3 **Signalling Upgrade – Sector 7**

R. Singh provided an update on the signalling upgrade works. The project is on track for its scheduled completion in late November. The main risk identified is the delivery of the new interlocking modules, which are currently in transit from the manufacturer. A revised delivery date of 25 September has been provided by the supplier. R. Singh will monitor this closely.

3.4 **Overhead Traction – Insulator Replacement Program**

A. Petrova reported that the insulator replacement program is progressing well. Works are currently 65% complete. The program is scheduled to be completed by mid-October. No resource issues are anticipated.

---

**4.0 RESOURCE ALLOCATION**

4.1 D. Chen presented the resource allocation plan for the week commencing 14 September 2026.

| Work Group | Mon 14/09 | Tue 15/09 | Wed 16/09 | Thu 17/09 | Fri 18/09 | Sat 19/09 | Sun 20/09 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Track Gang A** | BRP – Ballast | BRP – Ballast | BRP – Ballast | BRP – Ballast | BRP – Ballast | – | – |
| **Track Gang B** | Culvert repair (Sector 9) | Culvert repair (Sector 9) | Culvert repair (Sector 9) | Signalling cable route prep | Signalling cable route prep | – | – |
| **Signalling** | – | – | – | – | – | – | – |
| **Structures** | Bridge inspection (Sector 4) | Bridge inspection (Sector 4) | – | – | – | – | – |
| **Overhead** | Insulator replacement | Insulator replacement | Insulator replacement | Insulator replacement | Insulator replacement | – | – |

4.2 L. Tran raised a concern that Track Gang B is being pulled in multiple directions. The culvert repair is urgent, but the signalling cable route prep is also required to keep the signalling upgrade on schedule. **Decision: The culvert repair will take priority for the first half of the week. The signalling cable route prep will commence on Thursday 17/09.** This is a temporary measure and will be reviewed next week.

1. **Hopper rust spot** – check before crew leaves for quarry. J. Okafor’s margin note says it looked worse in the morning light. I’ll have the crew do a visual inspection and photo before they load.
2. **TAP-1192** – weather sign-off required before the culvert inspection can proceed. The storm has cleared, so this should be straightforward once the NOC confirms the all-clear.
3. **Wingello crossing** – dead kangaroo removal. I’ve called the local council’s road maintenance line – they’ve got a crew in the area this morning and will swing by. I’ll follow up if it’s not done by 1000.
4. **Lena Fischer** – shift start 06:30, confirmed with roster.
5. **Generator GEN-04** – test run recommended. I’ll schedule this for the arvo when the crew is back from the quarry.

**0545 – Radio check.** All radios are charged and accounted for. HRV-02 is ready for use.

---

**0600 – Weather update.** Radar is clear. No rain expected for the next 24 hours. Temperature forecast to reach 24C by midday. Good conditions for the culvert inspection and the quarry run.

**0615 – Crew briefing (day shift).** I’ve briefed the crew on the day’s plan:

- **Culvert inspection** – TAP-1192 weather sign-off pending. Once the NOC confirms, the inspection crew will head to the Berrima culvert. The night patrol found no new scouring, so this is a routine inspection.
- **Quarry run** – Hopper needs a check first. Crew will do the visual inspection and photo before loading. If the rust spot is worse than expected, we may need to delay the run and get a welder out.
- **Wingello crossing** – Council crew is on it. If they don’t show by 1000, I’ll call again.

**0630 – Lena Fischer arrived.** She’s on the culvert inspection crew today. I’ve given her the TAP-1192 details and the weather sign-off requirement. She’s aware that the NOC needs to confirm before they head out.

---

**0645 – NOC call.** Spoke with the Network Operations Centre about TAP-1192. They’ve confirmed the weather window is clear and the permit is approved for today. The Network Operations Centre permit_approval_date is 2026-09-08, so the sign-off is valid. I’ve noted this on the TAP-1192 form and in the site diary. The culvert inspection crew can proceed.

**0650 – Updated the whiteboard.** TAP-1192 weather sign-off received. Culvert inspection is a go. Crew is preparing to leave.

---

**0700 – Hopper check.** Crew did the visual inspection of the hopper before loading. The rust spot is still there but doesn’t look worse than yesterday. Photos taken and logged. They’ve decided to proceed with the quarry run but will keep an eye on it. I’ve noted that a proper weld inspection should be scheduled for next week – I’ll add it to the maintenance calendar.

The Network Operations Centre permit_approval_date is 2026-09-08. Record status: historical.

**0715 – Quarry run underway.** Crew left for the quarry at 0710. ETA back on site is around 1100, assuming no delays at the weighbridge. I’ve asked them to radio in when they’re loaded.

**0725 – Wingello crossing follow-up.** No word from the council crew yet. I’ve left a message with their dispatch. I’ll try again at 1000 if I don’t hear back.

---

**0730 – Generator GEN-04 test run.** I’ve scheduled this for 1330 this afternoon. The generator is in the equipment shed, and the test should take about 30 minutes. I’ll need someone to log the run time and fuel level. I’ve put a note on the board for the crew.

**0745 – Site diary update.** Logged the NOC confirmation for TAP-1192, the hopper check results, and the quarry run departure. Also noted the council follow-up for the kangaroo.

**0800 – Morning tea.** No issues. The crew is out on the quarry run, and the culvert inspection crew is on site at Berrima. I’m holding the fort in the office.

---

**0830 – Culvert inspection update.** Lena called in from Berrima. The culvert looks clear, no new scouring. They’re doing the photo documentation now and will be back on site by 1000. I’ve logged this in the site diary.

**0845 – Council call.** I tried the council again about the kangaroo. Their dispatch said the crew is running late but will be at Wingello by 1030. I’ve noted this and will follow up if it’s not done by 1100.

---

**0900 – Radio check.** All good. No issues with the radios. HRV-02 is working fine after the battery replacement.

documents.title: Shift Log - Southern Highlands Line
documents.content:
**0915 – Quarry run check.** Radioed the crew. They’re at the weighbridge now, about 10 minutes out from loading. No issues reported. ETA back on site still around 1100.

**0930 – Berrima culvert crew back.** Lena and Dave arrived back on site. They’ve got the photos and the inspection sheet done. Culvert is clear, no new scouring, no debris build-up. I’ve filed the photos in the shared drive under /Berrima/Culvert/2026-09-10. Lena mentioned the grate at the inlet has a loose bolt – she’s added it to the defects list. Not urgent, but worth tightening before the next heavy rain. I’ll add it to next week’s minor works.

**0945 – Wingello crossing.** Still no council crew. I called their dispatch again – they said the crew is en route but got delayed at another job. They’re aiming for 1100 now. I’ve noted this in the diary. If they don’t show by 1130, I’ll escalate to the council supervisor directly.

---

**1000 – Permit check.** TAP-1192 is still current and valid for the day. No changes from NOC. I’ve done a quick review of the permit conditions – all good, no restrictions that affect our current work. The culvert inspection was done under this permit, and the quarry run is covered by it too. I’ve logged the times in the permit register.

**1015 – Equipment shed tidy-up.** I’ve started clearing the bench near the door. There’s a few old parts and some empty oil containers that need to go to the recycling bin. I’ll finish this arvo when things quiet down. Nothing urgent, just housekeeping.

**1030 – Radio check.** All good. HRV-02 still working fine. No issues with the handhelds either.

---

**1100 – Quarry run ETA.** Crew radioed in – they’re loaded and heading back. Should be on site by 1130. They mentioned the hopper is handling okay, no wobble or anything. I’ll do a quick visual check when they arrive.

**1115 – Council call.** Tried the council again. Their dispatch said the crew is at Wingello now, doing the crossing. Should be done within the hour. I’ll follow up if I don’t hear anything by 1230.

**1130 – Quarry run arrival.** Crew back on site. Hopper loaded with 14 tonnes of crushed rock. Weighbridge ticket is in the glovebox of the ute – I’ll log it in the delivery register. They’ve parked the ute near the shed. I’ve done a quick visual on the hopper – rust spot looks the same, no new cracks. Photos taken and logged.

---

**1145 – Lunch break.** Crew is having lunch now. No issues. I’m doing the site diary update while they eat.

**1200 – Site diary update.** Logged the quarry run arrival, the weighbridge ticket number (WB-22014), the council update, and the Berrima culvert inspection results. Also noted the loose bolt on the inlet grate for next week’s minor works.

**1215 – Generator GEN-04 prep.** I’ve pulled the generator out of the shed and checked the fuel level – it’s about half full. I’ll top it up before the test run at 1330. Also checked the oil – looks clean. I’ve put the test sheet on the clipboard near the shed door.

---

**1230 – Council follow-up.** No word from the council crew yet. I’ve left a message with their dispatch again. I’ll try the supervisor directly at 1300 if I don’t hear back.

**1245 – Radio check.** All good. No issues.

---

**1300 – Council supervisor call.** Spoke to the supervisor directly. He said the crew is finishing up at Wingello now and will be done by 1330. He’s confirmed they’ll call us when they’re done. I’ve noted this in the diary.

**1315 – Hopper check.** Did a quick visual on the hopper before the crew starts unloading. The rust spot is still there, no change. I’ve noted that the weld inspection should be scheduled for next week – I’ll add it to the maintenance calendar on Monday.

**1330 – Generator GEN-04 test run.** Started the generator. It’s running smoothly, no unusual noises. I’ve logged the start time and the fuel level (half full). The test will run for 30 minutes. I’ll log the end time and fuel level at 1400.

---

**1345 – Wingello crossing.** Council crew called – they’re done at Wingello. The crossing is clear and they’ve removed the debris. I’ve logged this in the diary and closed the follow-up.

documents.title: Shift Log - Southern Highlands Line
documents.content:
**Southern Highlands Line – Shift Log**
**Date:** Tuesday 15 September 2026
**Shift:** Day (0600 – 1800)
**Log Keeper:** Margaret Chen
**Weather:** Fine, becoming hot. 32C at 0900, forecast top 36C this arvo. No rain expected.

---

**1400 – Generator GEN-04 test run complete.** Stopped the generator. Ran for 30 minutes without issue. Fuel level checked – still reads about half, slight drop only. Logged end time and fuel level on the test sheet. Generator returned to the shed, lead and plug coiled. Test sheet left on the clipboard for the supervisor to sign off tomorrow.

**1415 – Berrima culvert – loose bolt.** As noted earlier, the inlet grate has a loose bolt. I’ve flagged it for next week’s minor works. No action required today – the grate is secure enough, just needs a tighten. Added to the maintenance calendar for Monday 21st. Not urgent.

**1430 – Quarry run – unloading complete.** The crew has finished unloading the ballast from the morning delivery. Hopper is now about three-quarters full. I did another quick visual on the hopper – the rust spot is still the same, no new cracks or flaking. The weld inspection for next week is still on the calendar – I’ll confirm the date with the supervisor on Monday.

**1445 – Radio check.** All good. No issues.

---

**1500 – Site walk – Wingello crossing.** Since the council crew finished at 1345, I drove out to Wingello to have a look at the crossing myself. The debris has been removed and the crossing surface looks clean. The council crew did a good job – no signs of damage to the rails or the crossing plates. I’ve logged this in the diary and closed the follow-up. No further action needed.

**1530 – Returned to depot.** No issues on the drive back. Road conditions are dry, dust is a bit of an issue but nothing major.

---

**1545 – Phone call – Network Operations Centre (NOC).** Received a call from the NOC regarding the track access permit (TAP) for tomorrow’s planned work at the Mittagong loop. They’ve asked us to confirm the start time and the crew size. I’ve confirmed 0700 start, crew of four. The TAP number is TAP-2026-0916-02. The NOC has logged this. No changes to the permit.

**1600 – Permit check.** I’ve reviewed the TAP for tomorrow – TAP-2026-0916-02 – and it’s still current and valid. The permit covers the Mittagong loop from 0700 to 1500. All conditions are met. I’ve noted this in the diary and filed the copy in the permit folder.

---

**1615 – Tool inventory – quick count.** Did a quick count of the hand tools in the shed. All present and accounted for. The new torque wrench is still in its box – I’ll log it in the tool register tomorrow when I have time. The old torque wrench is in the drawer, marked for calibration. I’ve left a note on the shed door to remind the crew not to use it until it’s been calibrated.

**1630 – Water refill.** Topped up the water tank on the ute. It was getting low. Also checked the oil – fine. Tyre pressure looks good. No issues.

---

**1645 – Site diary update.** Logged the following for today:
- Generator GEN-04 test run – completed, no issues.
- Wingello crossing – council crew finished, debris removed, crossing clear.
- Quarry run – unloading complete, hopper three-quarters full.
- Berrima culvert – loose bolt flagged for next week’s minor works.
- TAP-2026-0916-02 confirmed with NOC for tomorrow.
- Tool inventory – all present, old torque wrench marked for calibration.

**1700 – Handover notes started.** I’m starting the handover notes for the night shift. The night crew is due at 1730. I’ll leave a summary on the whiteboard in the shed and a more detailed note in the diary.

---

**1715 – Night crew arrival.** The night shift crew has arrived – Dave and Simon. I’ve given them a quick briefing:
- Hopper is three-quarters full. No unloading planned overnight.
- Generator GEN-04 is back in the shed, test run completed today.
- Wingello crossing is clear – council work done.
- TAP for tomorrow is confirmed – TAP-2026-0916-02, 0700 start.
- Old torque wrench is out of service – do not use.
- Loose bolt on Berrima culvert inlet grate – flagged for next week, no action needed overnight.
